description: NASA's Black Marble products, described on the Earthdata project page read on 2026-09-26, use the VIIRS Day/Night Band to give a long-term record of global nighttime light composites at daily, monthly and yearly resolution. The VNP46 products from Suomi NPP start on 19 January 2012 and VJ146 from NOAA-20 on 5 January 2018, with VJ246 from NOAA-21; corrections for atmosphere, terrain, lunar reflectance and stray light yield surface radiance, and products are available in near real time within three hours. The page lists 17 datasets distributed by LAADS DAAC, with University of Maryland and NASA Goddard as principal investigators. Applications named include disaster response, monitoring energy access and changes in urban energy infrastructure, gas flares and socio-economic proxies. Data are free under NASA's open science policy in HDF-EOS5 format. Caveats: the page announces that delivery of Suomi NPP products ends on 1 November 2026, so users should move to NOAA-20 and NOAA-21 products; clouds and moonlight affect daily values. Simulation uses are mapping power outages and tracking restoration after disasters for resilience studies and emergency response. Related records: data-viirs-nightfire-gas-flaring-eog uses the same sensor for gas flares.
